title: Google Gemma passes one billion downloads, 100,000 published variants
subtitle: The first cumulative total Google has put on its open-weight family since launch in early 2024 — plus a new Awesome Gemma repository as the official Gemmaverse index.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Google DeepMind said its Gemma family of open-weight models passed one billion cumulative downloads, with outside developers publishing more than 100,000 variants — fine-tunes, quantizations, and adaptations for specific languages, tasks, and hardware. VP Clement Farabet and product director Olivier Lacombe disclosed the numbers on the Google blog on August 20. It is the first time Google has attached a cumulative total to Gemma adoption since the family debuted in early 2024. Google paired the announcement with a new Awesome Gemma repository on GitHub, curated as the official index of what it calls the Gemmaverse.

The 100,000-variant figure is the more revealing number. It measures actual downstream work rather than one-click downloads. Gemma variants are being used across healthcare imaging, space-based image analysis, low-resource-language chatbots, and even research on dolphin vocalizations. That kind of long tail is the argument open-weight advocates have been making since Llama 2 — that the community will build in places a single vendor never would — and Google now has two years of data to back it.

The milestone lands in an open-weights race that has intensified sharply this year. Meta reopened with Muse Glimmer under Apache 2.0 on August 10. Alibaba's Qwen family passed Meta and Google on some open benchmarks earlier this month. Moonshot's Kimi K3 and DeepSeek V4-Pro are pushing frontier-scale open models. Google's disclosure is a reminder that Gemma is not just a smaller-scale offering — it is the largest deployed base of any open model family, by download count.

For learners: if you are starting an LLM project on your own machine, search the Awesome Gemma repo before you fine-tune from scratch. The odds are very high that someone has already trained the variant you need, and the community's collective work will be better than what a single beginner run will produce.
